implementation_notes: Bunny wraps AMQP 0-9-1 in idiomatic Ruby: ch.queue("orders", durable: true).subscribe(manual_ack: true, prefetch: 10) { |delivery_info, properties, payload| ... } runs the consumer on the connection's consumer thread, and the endpoint is the block plus a small object that owns connection, channel and queue declarations. Karafka is the corresponding library when the broker is Kafka; the classic endpoint structure is not replaced by a language feature, so it should live in its own class (or service object) instead of inline in a script.
code_sketch:
conn = Bunny.new(ENV.fetch("AMQP_URL"))
conn.start
ch = conn.create_channel
q  = ch.queue("orders", durable: true)
q.subscribe(manual_ack: true, prefetch: 10) do |delivery_info, _properties, payload|
  handle(JSON.parse(payload))
  ch.ack(delivery_info.delivery_tag)
end
pitfalls: The subscribe block runs on the connection's consumer thread: an exception can tear down the channel, so rescue, log and reject the delivery instead of letting it escape.
Long blocking work in the block throttles that connection; scale by adding connections or processes rather than threads sharing one consumer.
Without manual_ack plus an explicit ack, Bunny's default auto-ack behaviour turns a crashed handler into a lost message.
